papers.title: Supporting Data Center Grid Integration via Co-Optimized Battery Energy Storage Sizing and Capacity Allocation
papers.abstract: Interconnecting large data centers can be delayed by grid requirements on demand flexibility, ramping limits, and ride-through performance. This paper proposes an optimization-based framework to size a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) that accelerates data center grid integration by providing BESS capacity required to meet selected flexibility and grid-support requirements. The model co-optimizes BESS power rating and energy capacity while allocating capability across three services: (i) demand response over a specified duration, (ii) mitigation of high-magnitude, high-frequency load fluctuations through reserved active power with zero net state-of-charge change, and (iii) voltage support via reactive power capability at the point of common coupling. Minute-level operational scheduling enforces state-of-charge feasibility and load ramp constraints, and incorporates a controllable queue of delay-insensitive computing tasks to enhance flexibility. A case study using a real data center load profile demonstrates the proposed method and quantifies the BESS power-energy requirements and operational trade-offs needed to satisfy the multi-service constraints, providing practical guidance for interconnection planning and deployment.

papers.title: Generalized H matrix stability for power systems
papers.abstract: The small-signal stability of a power system model with arbitrary loads is investigated, with a focus on locally constant power loads in lossless networks. A central element of the proposed analysis is the matrix H, which represents the partial derivatives of generator powers with respect to their relative angles. The local stability of any equilibrium point is determined by the properties of H if the loads consume locally constant power. Specifically, an equilibrium point is asymptotically stable if H is positive definite and unstable if H is full-rank and not positive definite, while several quantitative relationships between the eigenvalues of H and the system Jacobian matrix are also established. The main contribution is that loads are allowed to be arbitrarily located within the transmission network, thereby generalizing the existing H matrix stability criterion which is valid only if loads are located at the same buses as the generators. The advantage of the proposed criterion is demonstrated through case studies involving systems with up to 2869 buses. Accurate stability assessments are maintained, where alternative methods, such as the NRPS model, are found to be overly conservative. Additionally, a computational acceleration by a factor of 340 relative to Jacobian-based methods is achieved.

papers.title: Joint Electricity Price and Load Forecasting for Data Center Battery Dispatch Using Polynomial Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of large-scale data centers (DCs) is increasing electricity demand, market volatility, and operating costs. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) can mitigate these challenges by shifting electricity purchases from high-price to low-price periods. This paper proposes a real-time BESS dispatch framework using polynomial diffusion models (PDMs) to forecast both electricity prices and DC loads. Leveraging the closed-form conditional expectations of PDMs, the forecasts are integrated into a dynamic programming (DP) framework to minimize electricity procurement costs. Across the evaluated BESS configurations, the proposed approach achieves 2.63 times the cost savings of a rule-based (RB) strategy.

papers.title: Residential Vehicle-to-Grid Deployment: A United States-Based Stakeholder Perspective
papers.abstract: The integration of vehicle-to-grid (V2G), in which electric vehicle (EV) owners can send electricity from their vehicles back to the grid, is an emerging solution to enhance grid resilience. However, V2G deployment in the United States lags behind many other countries. This can be attributed to a broad range of factors, and to investigate them, this study analyzes semi-structured interviews with stakeholders using inductive-deductive qualitative coding. Results from the interviews are coded across financial, technical, social, political, and organizational dimensions in order to understand the three main deployment factors of drivers, benefits, and barriers of V2G. Once coded, the relationships between these factors are used to construct a cognitive map to identify actions that will most effectively drive V2G deployment. The results indicate that grid resilience and decarbonization are seen as the main benefits of V2G. User willingness to participate, a lack of technological readiness and standardization, prohibitive costs, and unsupportive laws and policies are among the most frequently cited barriers. Connections in the cognitive map indicate that the most closely related drivers for mitigating these barriers are user compensation for battery degradation, community outreach, the creation of grid interconnection standards and protocols, and supportive grants and policy frameworks for V2G piloting and adoption.

papers.title: Supporting Data Center Grid Integration via Co-Optimized Battery Energy Storage Sizing and Capacity Allocation
papers.abstract: Interconnecting large data centers can be delayed by grid requirements on demand flexibility, ramping limits, and ride-through performance. This paper proposes an optimization-based framework to size a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) that accelerates data center grid integration by providing BESS capacity required to meet selected flexibility and grid-support requirements. The model co-optimizes BESS power rating and energy capacity while allocating capability across three services: (i) demand response over a specified duration, (ii) mitigation of high-magnitude, high-frequency load fluctuations through reserved active power with zero net state-of-charge change, and (iii) voltage support via reactive power capability at the point of common coupling. Minute-level operational scheduling enforces state-of-charge feasibility and load ramp constraints, and incorporates a controllable queue of delay-insensitive computing tasks to enhance flexibility. A case study using a real data center load profile demonstrates the proposed method and quantifies the BESS power-energy requirements and operational trade-offs needed to satisfy the multi-service constraints, providing practical guidance for interconnection planning and deployment.

papers.title: Generalized H matrix stability for power systems
papers.abstract: The small-signal stability of a power system model with arbitrary loads is investigated, with a focus on locally constant power loads in lossless networks. A central element of the proposed analysis is the matrix H, which represents the partial derivatives of generator powers with respect to their relative angles. The local stability of any equilibrium point is determined by the properties of H if the loads consume locally constant power. Specifically, an equilibrium point is asymptotically stable if H is positive definite and unstable if H is full-rank and not positive definite, while several quantitative relationships between the eigenvalues of H and the system Jacobian matrix are also established. The main contribution is that loads are allowed to be arbitrarily located within the transmission network, thereby generalizing the existing H matrix stability criterion which is valid only if loads are located at the same buses as the generators. The advantage of the proposed criterion is demonstrated through case studies involving systems with up to 2869 buses. Accurate stability assessments are maintained, where alternative methods, such as the NRPS model, are found to be overly conservative. Additionally, a computational acceleration by a factor of 340 relative to Jacobian-based methods is achieved.

papers.title: Joint Electricity Price and Load Forecasting for Data Center Battery Dispatch Using Polynomial Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of large-scale data centers (DCs) is increasing electricity demand, market volatility, and operating costs. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) can mitigate these challenges by shifting electricity purchases from high-price to low-price periods. This paper proposes a real-time BESS dispatch framework using polynomial diffusion models (PDMs) to forecast both electricity prices and DC loads. Leveraging the closed-form conditional expectations of PDMs, the forecasts are integrated into a dynamic programming (DP) framework to minimize electricity procurement costs. Across the evaluated BESS configurations, the proposed approach achieves 2.63 times the cost savings of a rule-based (RB) strategy.

papers.title: Residential Vehicle-to-Grid Deployment: A United States-Based Stakeholder Perspective
papers.abstract: The integration of vehicle-to-grid (V2G), in which electric vehicle (EV) owners can send electricity from their vehicles back to the grid, is an emerging solution to enhance grid resilience. However, V2G deployment in the United States lags behind many other countries. This can be attributed to a broad range of factors, and to investigate them, this study analyzes semi-structured interviews with stakeholders using inductive-deductive qualitative coding. Results from the interviews are coded across financial, technical, social, political, and organizational dimensions in order to understand the three main deployment factors of drivers, benefits, and barriers of V2G. Once coded, the relationships between these factors are used to construct a cognitive map to identify actions that will most effectively drive V2G deployment. The results indicate that grid resilience and decarbonization are seen as the main benefits of V2G. User willingness to participate, a lack of technological readiness and standardization, prohibitive costs, and unsupportive laws and policies are among the most frequently cited barriers. Connections in the cognitive map indicate that the most closely related drivers for mitigating these barriers are user compensation for battery degradation, community outreach, the creation of grid interconnection standards and protocols, and supportive grants and policy frameworks for V2G piloting and adoption.
